title: contract-gap-review
description: Structured second-line contract gap matrix. Carries per-clause coverage, severity, recommended-amendment posture, legal-review triggers, and the open questions a control owner needs before signature, renewal, or amendment. Downstream consumers: vendor-diligence (reads the rollup into contract_gap_summary and contract_gap_record_id), exit-plan (reads the termination, transitional-support, and data-return findings), dora-register-builder (reads the mandatory-clause coverage flags), concentration-risk-review (reads the sub-contracting and change-of-control findings).

arrangement_id.description: Stable identifier for the vendor arrangement. Reused across criticality-assessment, vendor-diligence, exit-plan, and concentration-risk-review.

contract_identifier.description: MSA / SOW / order-form reference, including addenda where material to the matrix.

engagement_id.description: Optional pointer to the scope record under which this matrix was produced.

as_of_date.description: Date the gap matrix was last revised.

review_type.description: Why this matrix is being produced. Drives depth and review-gate set.

vendor_legal_name.description: Counterparty legal entity. Use the contracting entity, not the brand.

vendor_brand_name.description: Brand or product name if it differs from the legal entity.

service_type.description: Concise service description (cloud IaaS, foundation-model API, claims TPA, ACH processor, sub-adviser, etc.).

business_process_supported.description: Name of the firm's business process or important business service the contract supports.

important_business_service.description: If the firm has an IBS map, the IBS the arrangement sits in.

criticality.description: Sourced from criticality-assessment. The matrix consumes; it does not set.

criticality_source.description: Pointer to the criticality-assessment record, or 'inline' if set in this matrix.

data_access.description: Categories of firm or customer data the vendor touches under the contract.

data_locations.description: Regions where data is processed or stored under the contract. ISO country codes or named cloud regions.

cross_border_flows.description: True if the contract permits or requires customer or firm data to cross a regulated border.

ai_vendor.description: Gates the AI-clause cluster. True when the vendor supplies an AI system or AI-adjacent capability the firm relies on for inference, generation, classification, or autonomous action.

dora_in_scope.description: True when the arrangement is in scope of the EU digital-operational-resilience act as a critical-or-important-function ICT service. Gates the mandatory-clause overlay.

sector_overlay_set.description: Sector overlays loaded for this matrix.

cross_cutting_overlay_set.description: Cross-cutting overlays loaded for this matrix.

clauses.description: Clause-by-clause findings. One record per clause topic the loaded overlays raise.

mandatory_clauses.description: Mandatory-clause overlay findings. Required when dora_in_scope is true. Absence of any of these rows is by source a high-severity finding.

change_notification_days.description: Days of notice the contract requires for sub-processor change. Free-form to allow 'silent', 'reasonable period', or numeric.

termination_findings.description: Aggregated termination, exit, and assignment findings.

liability_findings.description: Aggregated liability, indemnity, and insurance findings.

limit_of_liability_cap_level.description: Cap level expressed in the contract's terms (e.g., 'one year fees', 'fixed amount', 'unlimited for carve-outs').

audit_findings.description: Aggregated audit, reporting, and regulator-access findings.

open_questions_for_counsel.description: Specific questions for legal and the contract owner. Each question names the clause row it relates to and the decision it supports.

reviewer_questions.description: Questions clustered for the forum that decides. Each question names the decision it supports.

legal_review_triggers.description: Specific clauses where counsel must redline before signature, tied to severity and firm policy.

summary_severity.description: Highest individual-clause severity, lifted by aggregation when two or more medium findings concentrate in a single cluster (audit, termination, incident-notification).

recommended_posture.description: The matrix's recommended posture. Final decision sits with counsel and the named approver, not the skill.

recommended_conditions.description: If redline-and-sign or redline-and-defer-decision, the conditions the vendor or firm must meet.

review_gates.description: Named human-review gates this matrix must clear. Drawn from references/review-gates.md.

next_review_trigger.description: Renewal date, scope-change trigger, regulatory-change-driven trigger, or model-version-change for AI vendors.

owner.description: Role, not person. Examples: third-party risk manager, contract owner, head of TPRM.

approver.description: Role of the human approver named in the firm's third-party-risk policy for this criticality tier.

counsel_of_record.description: Role of the counsel reviewing the redlines. In-house or external.

confidence_label.description: Confidence in the overall gap-matrix read, per references/review-gates.md.

source_trace.description: Citations supporting material findings. Every finding should be traceable.

clause_id.description: Stable ID for the clause record within this matrix.

clause_topic.description: What the clause is about. e.g., 'Subcontracting', 'Cybersecurity event notification', 'Audit rights', 'Termination for cause'.

source_criterion.description: The named regulatory or policy expectation. Cite by file path into references/source-anchors.md or an overlay; do not restate excerpts.

contract_reference.description: Section, clause, or schedule number in the contract. Use 'silent' if the contract is silent on the topic.

coverage.description: Coverage status of the clause against the source criterion.

gap_rationale.description: Plain-language explanation of why coverage was scored as it was. Cites contract phrasing where load-bearing.

recommended_amendment_posture.description: Posture for the redline, not legal language. Examples: 'tighten notification window from reasonable-period to 48 hours upstream of NYDFS 72-hour clock'; 'add sub-processor change-notice with rejection rights'; 'add Bank Service Company Act §1867(c) examiner-access continuity through wind-down'.

severity.description: Severity assessed against the criticality tier and the regulatory frame.

legal_review_required.description: True when the clause needs counsel redlines before signature or amendment.
